title: Latent transition learning maps short-term changes in Parkinson clinical profiles
summary: A probabilistically learned latent-transition model followed 250 people with Parkinson disease across two clinical assessments about 2.5 years apart. Most retained their model-defined profile, while a fourth severe multidomain profile emerged at follow-up and included a high proportion with dementia. These are observational clinical groupings and transitions, without established biological subtypes or lifetime convergence trajectories.
ai_technology: Latent class mixture learning; latent transition analysis in Mplus

source_review.scope: Read original primary latent-class/transition model fitting, measurement-invariance and missing-data Methods, cohort exclusions, class-transition Results, dementia enrichment and observational limitations. Learned non-neural mixture inference is the qualifying model operation; author use of the word AI is not required. Exact canonical online date October25 retained. Exact primary identity/date and fresh primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Eleven motor, cognitive and psychiatric indicators defined learned latent classes. Mplus latent-transition models compared three- and four-class follow-up structures using likelihood-based fit, information criteria and entropy; the selected model had three baseline and four follow-up classes. Among 250 analytic participants, 190 retained their class over a mean 2.51 years. The severe multidomain follow-up class had dementia in 64%, versus at most 7% in the other classes. Available autopsy information supported exclusion of nine non-Parkinson diagnoses before the analytic cohort was formed.
evidence.unknown: Only two assessment times and a predominantly White, non-Hispanic cohort constrain trajectory interpretation. Classes are data-dependent clinical profiles, not validated biological taxonomy. Dementia-related indicators contribute to the learned profiles, so dementia enrichment is not independent diagnostic validation. Same-cohort class transitions and secondary regression associations do not establish causal progression, universal eventual convergence, independent forecasting or treatment benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Probabilistic latent-mixture and transition learning estimated multidomain classes and membership transitions from clinical measurements; these learned representations enabled the reported stability and emergent severe-profile finding. Conventional secondary logistic regression is not the enabling AI claim.
